set.descent_text: The gully above the technical climbing leads on toward the summit area, but most parties bail off to the right across the top of the Corinthian Column and walk back to the road and car. Spring avalanche danger on this face is real, so check the forecast before committing.
set.approach: Park at the last big bend of the Pikes Peak toll road, below the final climb to the summit, cross the road and walk east a short way, then drop onto the Hero Traverse (also called the Hero Rock Traverse). This descends at first, then traverses southeast around snow gullies and a spur to a broad amphitheater and the Corinthian Column, a big rock buttress. Total Abandon takes the gully and chimney system on the right side of the column. Parties unfamiliar with the traverse should allow about an hour, and the whole walk-in is short compared with most alpine ice.

review.notes: Road start, Hero Traverse, Corinthian Column and right-side chimney from route and area pages; short walk-in from AAJ article; bail right to the car from route page and neighbours.

set.descent_text: The chimney finishes toward the summit snowfields. Most parties break sharply right near the top, cross over the top of Total Abandon and follow the ridge back toward the car. Rappelling the route is also done.
set.approach: Park at the last big bend of the Pikes Peak toll road, below the final climb to the summit, cross the road and walk east a short way, then drop onto the Hero Traverse (also called the Hero Rock Traverse). This descends at first, then traverses southeast around snow gullies and a spur to a broad amphitheater and the Corinthian Column, a big rock buttress. Walk across the snowfield past the base of Total Abandon to the far side of the column, turn right and go uphill to the chimney on its left side. Two fixed pitons on the gully's left wall mark the first belay.

review.notes: Approach and walk-off from the route page; walk-off right over Total Abandon and the rappel option agree on Blind Luck and The Ole 6 pages.

set.descent_text: After the last short pitch the technical difficulty ends. Walk off to the right across the tops of Blind Assumption and Total Abandon and continue to the highway. Rappelling Blind Assumption is the alternative.
set.approach: Park at the last big bend of the Pikes Peak toll road, below the final climb to the summit, cross the road and walk east a short way, then drop onto the Hero Traverse (also called the Hero Rock Traverse). This descends at first, then traverses southeast around snow gullies and a spur to a broad amphitheater and the Corinthian Column, a big rock buttress. Blind Luck winds around Blind Assumption, on the column's left flank. Its first pitch follows that of Blind Assumption, so find the chimney start there; the line stops short below a large chockstone.

review.notes: Route page for walk-off and start; Blind Assumption page for the shared first pitch; AAJ article places it on the left side of the column.

set.descent_text: The third pitch finishes on a ledge even with where Total Abandon ends. A simple scramble reaches the walk-off ledge that Total Abandon parties use, and from there you return to the road and car.
set.approach: Park at the last big bend of the Pikes Peak toll road, below the final climb to the summit, cross the road and walk east a short way, then drop onto the Hero Traverse (also called the Hero Rock Traverse). This descends at first, then traverses southeast around snow gullies and a spur to a broad amphitheater and the Corinthian Column, a big rock buttress. The route takes the groove farthest left inside the alcove next to Total Abandon, on its right.

review.notes: Route page for location and top-out; Furloughed page places it left of its own line and uses the same exit as Total Abandon.

set.descent_text: After the final pitch, easy snow and turf lead to the top. Climb a little higher and leave by the exit Total Abandon uses, which returns you to the road.
set.approach: Park at a pullout on the Pikes Peak toll road, cross the road and hike across the Hero Traverse toward the Corinthian Column. The route is on the Sunshine Wall, which sits to the right of the column, beyond both Total Abandon and 66 Years of Fun. Climb easy snow to the base below 66 Years of Fun, then traverse right over slab to the start.

review.notes: Single route page for its own position; area and Total Abandon pages confirm the Hero Traverse approach and exit.

set.descent_text: Climb the remaining easy snow toward the summit and stop at the shoulder just short of it, where the hikers' trail leads down.
set.approach: Take the Hero Traverse from the toll road as for the Y Couloir, passing Total Abandon and Blind Assumption. Look for a gap in the rock band between Blind Assumption and the Y Couloir. The route starts on a snow cone below a rocky constriction.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent; Y Couloir page confirms Hero Traverse access.

set.descent_text: The last pitch is broken ground to the top of the Corinthian Column. From there the usual walk-off is to scramble up the buttress and head off to the right toward the highway.
set.approach: Park at the last big bend of the Pikes Peak toll road, below the final climb to the summit, cross the road and walk east a short way, then drop onto the Hero Traverse (also called the Hero Rock Traverse). This descends at first, then traverses southeast around snow gullies and a spur to a broad amphitheater and the Corinthian Column, a big rock buttress. Three Dragons takes the steepest line up the middle of the column, halfway between Blind Assumption and Total Abandon beneath an obvious roof system.

review.notes: Route page for position and top-out; walk-off from neighbouring column routes.

set.descent_text: The roof traverse ends on or just below the top of the buttress. Either rappel Blind Assumption, or scramble up the buttress and walk off to the right toward the highway.
set.approach: Park at the last big bend of the Pikes Peak toll road, below the final climb to the summit, cross the road and walk east a short way, then drop onto the Hero Traverse (also called the Hero Rock Traverse). This descends at first, then traverses southeast around snow gullies and a spur to a broad amphitheater and the Corinthian Column, a big rock buttress. The Ole 6 is on the big buttress left of Total Abandon. Its line is the clear corner system capped by a large roof.

review.notes: Route page; AAJ article puts it on the Corinthian Column.

set.descent_text: After a mossy top-out, scramble up a short way, then cross right over the top of Total Abandon to return to the road and car.
set.approach: Park at the last big bend of the Pikes Peak toll road, below the final climb to the summit, cross the road and walk east a short way, then drop onto the Hero Traverse (also called the Hero Rock Traverse). This descends at first, then traverses southeast around snow gullies and a spur to a broad amphitheater and the Corinthian Column, a big rock buttress. Toga Party lies on the Corinthian Column, to the right of the large roof near the top. The first pitch begins where the gully below The Ole 6's right-facing corners starts.

review.notes: Route page; AAJ article places it on the right side of the column.

set.approach: The couloir starts from the Bottomless Pit below the north face. Three ways in are used: the long hike up the Barr Trail, a shorter but harder hike from the Crags trailhead, or a short descent from the toll road, which leaves no easy way back down. The Hero Traverse from the toll road also reaches the foot of the line. The line is obvious to the south; start up the main gully, and the Y branches west, to climber's right, after about a third of a mile.

review.notes: Route page for the three approaches and the branching; Guide's Couloir page confirms Hero Traverse access. Descent from the summit not described, so omitted.

set.descent_text: The couloir ends at a platform near the start of the Hero Traverse, which leads back to the toll road and the car. The traverse faces east and warms early, so factor that into the timing.

review.notes: Single route page; approach omitted because it refers to another route's approach.

set.descent_text: The couloir exits at the lip near the road, southeast of Little Pike's Peak, so the walk back to the car is short.
set.approach: Park just past Little Pike's Peak on the toll road, before the sheep sign. Follow the centre to southern part of Rumdoodle Ridge down to about 12,200 feet, then take the broad south-facing scree slope on your right to the base of the Bottomless Pit. Coming in this way keeps the objective in view and avoids leeward slopes. Cutting in from the southern flank is easy to get wrong and can leave you cliffed out. Avalanche awareness matters here; check the forecast.
